ASTR 101.description: An introduction to the solar system and universe accomplished with interactive lectures, demonstrations, and laboratory experience. Designed primarily for the non-science major.
ASTR 101.subject: ASTR
ASTR 101.title: Introduction to Astronomy

ASTR 103.description: Life beyond earth, search for habitable planets, search for extraterrestrial intelligence.
ASTR 103.subject: ASTR
ASTR 103.title: Astrobiology: Quest For Alien Life

ASTR 201.description: Astronomical topics including stellar death, black holes, dark matter, dark energy and cosmology. Astronomical techniques and application of the scientific method in astronomy.
ASTR 201.subject: ASTR
ASTR 201.title: Introduction to Astronomy II: The Dark Universe

ASTR 301.description: Galactic Astrophysics presents the physical processes for the formation, structure, and evolution of the Milky Way and the structure and properties of the interstellar medium.
ASTR 301.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ASTR 201 and PHYS 212.
ASTR 301.subject: ASTR
ASTR 301.title: Galactic Astrophysics

ASTR 302.description: Properties of normal and active galaxies, galaxy structures, galaxies at high redshifts, galaxy evolution.
ASTR 302.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ASTR 101 or SCHC 115; C or better in ASTR 201.
ASTR 302.subject: ASTR
ASTR 302.title: Extragalactic Astronomy

ASTR 320.description: Nature of the sun, planets; galactic and extragalactic sources at radio wavelengths; quasars; techniques, detectors, and telescopes.
ASTR 320.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ASTR 201; C or better in MATH 115 or equivalent; C or better in PHYS 202 or PHYS 212.
ASTR 320.subject: ASTR
ASTR 320.title: Introduction to Radio Astronomy

ASTR 340.description: Final states of stellar evolution; white dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes. Cosmology.
ASTR 340.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ASTR 201; C or better in MATH 115; C or better in PHYS 202 or PHYS 212.
ASTR 340.subject: ASTR
ASTR 340.title: Introduction to Relativistic Astrophysics

ASTR 499.description: Introduction to and application of the methods of research. A written report on work accomplished is required at the end of each semester.
ASTR 499.subject: ASTR
ASTR 499.title: Undergraduate Research

ASTR 510.description: Observational techniques, scientific method application, and astronomical data analysis taken from international telescopes.
ASTR 510.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: A minimum grade of C in CSCE 106 (Python) and ASTR 101 or ASTR 201; or graduate student standing.
ASTR 510.subject: ASTR
ASTR 510.title: Observational Astronomy

ASTR 533.description: Development of a combination of observational techniques and facility at reduction of data. A maximum of eight hours per week of observation, data reduction, and consultation. Offered each semester by arrangement with the department.
ASTR 533.subject: ASTR
ASTR 533.title: Advanced Observational Astronomy

ASTR 534.description: A continuation of ASTR 533 . Up to eight hours per week of observation, data reduction, and consultation.
ASTR 534.subject: ASTR
ASTR 534.title: Advanced Observational Astronomy

ASTR 546.description: The basics of observational techniques, structure and evolution of stars, interstellar medium and star formation, structure and properties of the Milky Way and nearby galaxies, and generation and transfer of radiation in astrophysical environments.
ASTR 546.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 307 or graduate student standing.
ASTR 546.subject: ASTR
ASTR 546.title: Introduction to Astrophysics

ASTR 599.description: Readings and research on selected topics in astronomy. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
ASTR 599.subject: ASTR
ASTR 599.title: Topics in Astronomy
